544862|2026-06.headline: Solex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.8% YoY to INR265.6 crore while PAT fell to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin) on higher depreciation and finance costs.
544862|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR265.6 crore, up 1.8% YoY from INR261 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR33.8 crore (12.7% margin vs 16.4%). Depreciation rose to INR10.2 crore and finance cost to INR12.5 crore, taking PAT to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin). Management attributed the weak quarter to seasonality, ALMM-2 (ALCM) timing shifts that delayed module off-take, and full-quarter costs of the 4 GW capacity, and reiterated FY27 guidance of a 5-6% PAT margin with an H2-weighted year. Management also flagged progress on a 2.2 GW cell line, with funding and land still pending.

financial_highlights.change: +1.8% YoY vs INR261 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR42.7 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR4.3 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Module manufacturing (4 GW, Tadkeshwar, Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Four module lines operating; lines 3 and 4 commissioned November 2025 and reached full utilisation by March 2026. FY27 average utilisation assumed at about 55%, versus about 70% in FY26 per an analyst question.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Not a focus; management targets INR100-150 crore of EPC business at a 10-12% margin, mainly C&I projects of 1-5 MW and rooftop. Government EPC revenue booked in Q1 FY26 was not repeated.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance and PAT margin of 5-6% reiterated.
FY27 module utilisation assumed at about 55% on average across the year.
Executable order pipeline of INR845.84 crore (INR628+ crore order from July, INR42.47 crore order from August, INR175 crore LOI with MSA at signing stage) targeted for execution by December 31, 2026.
2.2 GW N-type TOPCon+ cell line on track for commissioning by end of calendar 2027.
Vision 2030: 10 GW module, 10 GW cell, 10 GW BESS and 2 GW wafer/ingot capacity; INR4,000 crore MoU with Government of Gujarat.
Module capex reduced: planned 2.5 GW module line dropped; cell project cost now about INR1,050 crore (INR700 crore debt, INR350 crore equity via NCDs/CCDs).
capex_capacity: Module capacity 4 GW at Tadkeshwar, Gujarat; lines 3 and 4 commissioned November 2025.
2.2 GW cell line (phase 1 of 5 GW single-site cell plan; phase 2 of 3 GW). Commissioning targeted by end CY2027.

Cell project cost about INR1,050 crore: debt of about INR700 crore at advanced discussion with lender; equity of INR350 crore via NCDs/CCDs in due diligence. QIP/preferential route abandoned due to market conditions.
Land: parcel procured per management; 30 MW power connection in Gujarat has verbal approval, written approval awaited.
Cell technology partner and KPI-linked operator being onboarded for line design, commissioning and operations.
BESS: containerised manufacturing setup under evaluation with technology partners; to sit in a separate subsidiary. No timeline given beyond 'coming quarters'.
demand_pricing: Order book approximately INR3,400 crore (per management), across confirmed POs, signed MSAs awaiting POs, and advanced-stage MSAs; management says visibility is not contingent on ALMM-2 outcome.
ALMM-2 (ALCM) on cells: no extension announced on 25 May 2026, causing project holds and customer-driven delivery rescheduling in Q1 and Q2. Management calls these timing shifts, not cancellations.
Management estimated about 20% of orders have vulnerability from the captive/DCR segment; said this was resolved by the government's selective extension to December 2026 for commissioning.

Domestic DCR cell supply constrained: three Indian cell makers supply small volumes; one partner to supply 1 GW per year after ramp-up; total about 2.5 GW per year of G12R cells expected from MoU partners.
Export focus: Europe, Middle East, Africa, with US market being tested; FY27 export revenue projected to be low.
OEM/contract manufacturing for global brands under discussion; two global top-five brands already served; Q4 FY27 targeted for Indian projects.
Customer concentration: largest closed order above INR600 crore; second INR175 crore; third INR42 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the capex plan change from INR1,500 crore (INR1,100 crore cell, INR200 crore module, INR100 crore working capital) to INR1,050 crore cell project funded INR700 crore debt and INR350 crore equity, and which figure should be used for FY27 modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier plan included an additional 2.5 GW module line, which has been dropped given market conditions, reducing roughly INR200 crore. The current cell project cost is about INR1,050 crore for the 2.2 GW line: INR700 crore from principal lenders and INR350 crore as promoter margin.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory rose from INR1,795 million to INR2,905 million in FY26; is there obsolescence or write-down risk from technology change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the inventory build seasonal, with the same H1 pattern in FY26 and in the current period, and said the company makes the latest G12R generation, so no technology obsolescence impact. Inventory is expected to clear after monsoon; H2 vs H1 gap cited as roughly 1:3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 weak when historically Q1 is not this weak, and monsoon was delayed so execution should have been stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to lines 3 and 4 running with full interest and depreciation against lower revenue, and to absence of Q1 FY26 government EPC revenue. It attributed module delays to the ALMM-2 clarity gap, with the 1 June deadline and about 9,500 extension applications, and said orders are deferred, not cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is exposed to ALMM-2, and what cell supply arrangements exist for DCR orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most grandfathered projects are unaffected and about 20% of orders have vulnerability from the captive/DCR segment, now addressed by the extension to December 2026. Three Indian cell makers supply small volumes; one partner will supply 1 GW per year after ramp-up; about 2.5 GW per year of G12R cells is expected from MoU partners, mainly from next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the largest customer concentration and the EPC order book and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest closed order is above INR600 crore, second is INR175 crore (LOI, MSA at signing), third is INR42 crore from a domestic captive project. EPC is not a focus; target is INR100-150 crore at a 10-12% margin, mainly C&I projects of 1-5 MW and rooftop.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 module utilisation assumed at 55% versus about 70% in FY26 despite the larger 4 GW base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an industry average utilisation of about 50%, the ALMM-related disruption, and the domestic cell shortage, calling the 55% assumption conservative. Capacity rose from 1.5 GW to 4 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cell line status on land, power, and funding, and how does execution risk compare with peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Land parcel is procured per management; a 30 MW Gujarat power connection has verbal approval with written approval awaited. Debt of about INR700 crore is at advanced discussion; the INR350 crore equity via NCDs/CCDs is in due diligence; QIP/preferential route was dropped. The company said a TOPCon operator will be onboarded on a KPI-linked basis and that the 5 GW single site is being built in two phases.

risks_watch: ALMM-2 (cell) policy: no extension announced on 25 May 2026; captive/DCR orders depend on the December 2026 commissioning extension, and about 20% of orders are flagged as vulnerable.

Domestic DCR cell supply: only small volumes today, 1 GW per year from one partner after ramp-up, and about 2.5 GW per year of G12R cells expected from MoU partners, which are converting lines from G12 to G12R. Timing is uncertain.

Cell project funding and approvals: INR700 crore debt at advanced discussion, INR350 crore equity via NCDs/CCDs still in due diligence, and the 30 MW Gujarat power connection awaiting written approval. Commissioning is targeted for end-CY2027.
Working capital and finance cost: finance cost rose to INR12.5 crore from INR5.4 crore, with more reliance on fund-based limits. Inventory rose to INR2,905 million in FY26 from INR1,795 million.

Guidance credibility: FY27 PAT margin guidance of 5-6% against a Q1 PAT margin of 3.1%, with a 55% utilisation assumption and an H2-weighted year. Q2 is already seen following the same seasonal pattern.

Order book quality: the INR3,400 crore book mixes confirmed POs, signed MSAs awaiting POs and advanced MSAs; only the INR845.84 crore executable pipeline is targeted for execution by December 31, 2026. Track PO conversion next quarter.
Export and OEM diversification: FY27 export revenue is projected to be low. OEM work for global brands for Indian projects is targeted for Q4 FY27.
key_quotes: These are the timing shifts and not cancellations.
Investors should see Q1 as a near-term operating cycle and cell manufacturing as a medium-term earnings inflection.
We remain aligned with the FY27 revenue guidance and PAT margin in the range of 5% to 6%.
We will announce everything once the finance closure is done and then we get a confirmation from the electricity connection.
544862|2026-06.management_tone: Management is confident on the H2 recovery and the order book, but cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term numbers. It is firm that Q1 is seasonal and that ALMM-2 effects are timing rather than cancellations. It is less specific on cell-project funding and land timelines, and on BESS, where it gave no timeline.

rows.why: Cell project of about INR1,050 crore (INR700 crore debt, INR350 crore equity) is still pending lender approval and NCD/CCD due diligence, and the BESS setup has no timeline; the QIP route was abandoned, so a new capex announcement is conditional on funding closure rather than utilisation.

rows.why: Finance cost rose to INR12.5 crore from INR5.4 crore YoY, and the INR700 crore cell debt is still at advanced discussion, so interest costs are likely to stay high until the new line is commissioned end-CY2027.

544865|2026-06.headline: LEAP India Q1 FY27 total income rose 19% to INR2,134 million, EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million at a 53.5% margin.
544865|2026-06.overview: LEAP India, India's largest on-demand pallet pooling company, reported its maiden post-listing quarter with total income up 19% YoY to INR2,134 million and EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million. PAT rose 30% to INR247 million (12% margin) and cash PAT rose 23% to about INR812 million. Management reported 48 new customers in the quarter against a normal 15-20, asset count of 14.9 million, and utilisation up to 89.2%. Capex slowed to INR76 million-equivalent (stated as INR76 crores) from INR110 crores a year earlier as raw-material inflation made new crate and pallet purchases less attractive.

financial_highlights.change: up 1.26 million vs Q1 FY26 (13.65 million)
vs INR1.45 in same quarter last year

segments.name: Pallets (pooling)
segments.commentary: Pooled pallet count at around 9.2 million; management targets about 850,000 net additions in FY27 and says pooling growth of 17-18% YoY is achievable. Price increases of 5-6% were taken, linked to the German wood price index.

segments.name: Containers / crates
segments.commentary: Revenue growth of about 13% with asset additions of only 3-4%; management is deliberately slowing crate purchases because crate cost rose from about INR650 to INR1,000-1,200.

segments.name: MHE (TARON)
segments.commentary: 174 new machines added in Q1 and INR35.3 crores revenue (+33%); average monthly MHE pooling turnover rose from INR9.6 crores to INR11.6 crores. Management expects TARON to stay in a 14-17% growth bracket long-term.

segments.name: Middle East (GCC)
segments.commentary: Entities set up in Saudi Arabia (MISA licence), ADGM and Dubai; about five staff and about 20 customer discussions; Q1 capex in the region was held back due to the conflict. Management sees INR150-200 crores revenue in three years.

guidance_outlook: Management guides to about 20% YoY revenue growth (confirmed on the call as YoY, not QoQ), with GCC treated as additive to India growth.
EBITDA margin expected to stay within 47-56% for the next couple of quarters; management sees 100-200 bps potential margin expansion over time, but not a steady quarterly rise.
EBITDA growth expected to exceed revenue growth on a full-year basis, per management's answer to an analyst.
Target of about 3.7 million Movement Hire pallet moves in FY27, with 800,000-900,000 pallets added to the pooling model.
DSO expected to fall 10-15 days per quarter, with working capital normalising within two to three quarters.
Two more warehouses (about 250,000-300,000 sq ft) to be closed in Q2-Q3; a small 40,000-pallet pool may open in Silvassa.
Acquisition opportunities in India and abroad are at an early stage; management indicated updates in Q2-Q3.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 asset spend about INR76 crores vs INR110 crores in Q1 FY26; management is slowing purchases given input cost inflation and is repairing more (1.4 million pallets repaired in Q1 vs 1.2 million a year earlier).
Utilisation target: above 90-91% in the next quarter and 92%+ over the next couple of years; a buffer of about 900,000 pallets is available.
Movement Hire fleet of 400-plus lithium-ion battery forklifts and 140 machines ready for delivery; 1,440 forklifts in total.
Planned 3D printing for inserts and automated crate cleaning by next quarter.
Warehouse network reduced to 28 fulfilment centres after the CHEP integration; 10,500 touchpoints.
demand_pricing: 48 new customers in Q1 (normal run-rate 15-20), including Lear Automotive, Minda Instruments, Havells Logistics, Woodpecker, Green Agri and Sriram Foods; expected to add about 120,000 static-hire pallets.
Beverage and cola demand was extended by a late rainy season (Adhik Maas), shifting demand from March into April-May; this drove positive net pallet additions in Q1.
E-commerce and quick-commerce added about 25,000 pallets (Zomato, Blinkit) and 3PLs added about 30,000 (DP World, DHL, Yusen).
Textile was subdued due to raw-material shortages and cost increases; this reduced Movement Hire volumes.
Pricing: 5-6% annual price increases, linked to the German wood price index, are embedded in 3-5 year contracts; 24 contracts were renewed in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Asset growth was 9% but revenue rose 19%; how is the growth split between asset growth and throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth comes from churn; FY26 moved about 2.8 million pallets and FY27 is targeted at about 3.7 million. Movement Hire rose 8% and textile/other sectors contributed the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Can you guide to EBITDA margins for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins have ranged 47-56% over six to seven years; FY26 was 50.7% and Q1 was 53.5%. Management expects 47-56% for the next couple of quarters and does not expect steady quarterly expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ revenue growth on a YoY basis and is Middle East additive?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed YoY. Middle East is additive. Management expects INR150-200 crores of GCC revenue in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is container revenue growth modest at 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: No slowdown in demand; management is limiting purchases because crate costs rose sharply, and is retrieving existing assets faster.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pallet 'sales' revenue look up about 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sells pallets only selectively, to customers who will eventually return to pooling; it says this is not a core focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue uplift from static to Movement Hire?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-pallet yield is INR1.54 (about INR562 a year). Management says it could rise to INR600-712 as Movement Hire share increases from about 0.3x toward 0.5-0.6x, with no new assets needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Movement Hire only 0.3x in India and what would lift it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a fragmented truck market (about 1,000 body sizes) and recommended standardising to about 10. It said that when one large player adopts pooling, peers follow.

risks_watch: Middle East (GCC) ramp-up is delayed by the regional conflict; first pooling go-live slipped to mid-September after August intensification, and management says it has other levers within India to cover any shortfall.

Input-cost inflation in crates and timber: management is slowing crate purchases (INR76 crores vs INR110 crores), which could weigh on container asset growth and pallet additions if costs stay elevated.
Movement Hire growth of 8% lagged asset and revenue growth, with textile subdued by raw-material shortages; the FY27 target of about 3.7 million moves needs a sharp pickup in the back half.

Margin path: management guided EBITDA margin of 47-56% for the next couple of quarters and said quarterly expansion will not be steady, while also saying EBITDA growth will outpace 20%+ revenue growth; monitor how these reconcile as MHE mix rises.
Working capital: DSO fell to 119 days from 131 days; management expects 10-15 days reduction per quarter, with normalisation in two to three quarters. Track delivery against this.

Acquisitions are at an early stage in India and abroad; management indicated updates in Q2-Q3. Also watch related-party transaction commentary raised in the market, which management addressed on the call.
key_quotes: So, one, I believe that this is a bit of ignorance into the supply chain network.

We are going slow on that, and that is one of the reasons that in the first quarter also you will see that as compared to INR110 crores investment vis-a-vis last year, this year, we have just done INR76 crores.
But one thing I can very clearly tell you that it will hover around 47% to 56% margin for next couple of quarters.
Yes, Vijay, Middle East will be over and above business. That is what we are expecting.
544865|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, pooling growth, pricing and customer wins, with stated targets on 20%+ growth and 800,000-900,000 net pallet additions. Cautious on the Middle East (capex held back, go-live delayed) and on crate and container investment given input-cost inflation, and noncommittal on quarterly margin direction, which management said will not rise steadily.

rows.why: EBITDA margin guided at 47-56% for the next couple of quarters vs 53.5% in Q1 and FY26 at 50.7%; management sees 100-200 bps potential over time but explicitly not a steady quarterly rise, with MHE mix as a lever.

rows.why: Net pooled additions of about 850,000 pallets in FY27 on a 9.2m base, 174 MHE machines added in Q1, 140 more machines ready for delivery, and a 40,000-pallet Silvassa pool planned for Q2; GCC first go-live slipped to mid-September.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Movement Hire pallet moves targeted at 3.7m in FY27 vs 2.8m in FY26 (about 32% step-up) though Q1 Movement Hire grew only 8% to 766,000, so back-half pickup is needed; 48 new customers in Q1 vs 15-20 normal and utilisation at 89.2% with target of 90-91% next quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 89.2% (above the 80%+ threshold) with a buffer of only about 900,000 pallets, yet crate capex was cut to INR76 crore from INR110 crore and GCC capex was held back, so a new capex plan is conditional on input costs and the Middle East conflict.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 3D printing for inserts and automated crate cleaning planned by next quarter, and Middle East entities in Saudi Arabia, ADGM and Dubai are set up with INR150-200 crore revenue sought in three years; no firm product launch date given.

rows.label: 5-6% contract price escalation tied to German wood index
rows.when: embedded in 3-5 year contracts; 24 renewed in Q1
rows.why: Price increases of 5-6% are already in contracts and per-pallet yield rose to INR1.54 from INR1.45 (+6%).

rows.label: DSO normalisation
rows.why: DSO fell to 119 days from 131 days and management expects a 10-15 day reduction per quarter, normalising within two to three quarters.

rows.label: Middle East (GCC) go-live and ramp
rows.why: First pooling go-live slipped to mid-September after August conflict intensification, ~5 staff and ~20 customer discussions, with INR150-200 crore revenue sought in three years.

544865|2026-09.headline: LEAP India Q2 FY27 total income rose 23% YoY to INR2,159 mn and PAT rose 62% to INR178 mn, with EBITDA margin at 50.8%.
544865|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed continued growth: total income INR2,159 mn (+23% YoY), EBITDA INR1,097 mn (+25%) at a 50.8% margin, and PAT INR178 mn (+62%). Finance costs fell to INR215 mn after INR3,596 mn of IPO-funded debt repayment. Management announced the acquisition of Vimprotech (manufacturing) and TIPS (crate and tray pooling) for a combined equity value of INR142 crore, with revenue expected from November. Rating was upgraded to A+ by India Ratings, and GCC subsidiaries in Saudi Arabia and UAE are set up but not yet generating revenue. Movement hire volumes were about 720,000 in Q2, below management's earlier expectations, which management attributed to plastic (granule) price spikes hitting textile and automotive customers.

financial_highlights.change: +62% YoY (c.+109% excluding INR65 mn... management cited INR6.5 crore prepayment break cost)
Reduced after INR3,596 mn debt repayment
from 128 days at start of year

segments.name: Asset pooling (pallets, containers, crates)
segments.commentary: Income INR1,759 mn in Q2, +19% YoY. Pallets contribute about 64% of revenue, automotive crates/containers about 20-22%, per management.

segments.name: Material handling equipment (TARON)
segments.commentary: Income INR393 mn in Q2, +52% YoY (management also cited 60% revenue growth), with EBITDA up about 28%; TARON EBITDA margin cited at about 30%, around 14-16% of revenue; about 150 machines deployed.

segments.name: GCC (Saudi Arabia, UAE)
segments.commentary: Wholly owned subsidiaries set up with licences obtained; spend so far about INR2.5-3 crore; 26 customers in touch; revenue expected to start as early as next month, with management promising numbers next quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR918-920 crore, with about 50% EBITDA margin and PAT of about INR90 crore (per management in Q&A).
Management said PAT growth could be 60-80% in FY27 versus its prior 40-44% framing; FY26 PAT cited as about INR62 crore.
Movement hire target of 3.6-3.7 million transfer hire movements for FY27; Q2 delivered about 720,000 (1.5 million in H1 per management).
Pallet utilisation target of 90-91% over coming quarters from 89.3% in Q2.
FY27 capex guidance of about INR450 crore; H1 capex INR213 crore versus INR201 crore in H1 FY26.
DSO target below 90 days by end of FY27 from 122 days.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex INR213 crore versus INR201 crore in H1 FY26; FY27 full-year capex guided at about INR450 crore.
Asset base 15.5 million versus 13.8 million a year ago; 417,000 net pallets added in the period to September.
Pallet utilisation 89.3% (flat YoY); container utilisation 73.7% (from 71.7%); MHE utilisation 82.3%.
Network consolidated to 27 fulfilment centres after closing two facilities from CHEP integration.
Vimprotech has two plants (Puducherry and Tamil Nadu) with two lines, currently able to meet about 50% of LEAP's plastic needs; management aims for 100% in-house over time.
Plinova (timber sourcing subsidiary) controls timber cost; average pallet cost about INR1,750.
demand_pricing: Pallet yield per pallet rose to INR1.54 per day from INR1.46-1.48 previously; management implies about INR562-565 annual revenue per pallet at around 50% EBITDA.
Automotive demand exceeds supply: customers requested 4 crates and received about 1.5; 200,000 crates added in Q2 after raw material cost eased to about USD90 level.
Granule and plastic costs spiked (crude above USD120 per management), hurting textile (operating at about 20% capacity per management) and plastic goods customers, slowing movement hire conversions.
Pallet movement hire: 720,000 movements in Q2 (rainy season); management expects about 34% of annual volume in Dec-Mar.
Customer additions: 85 in H1 (LEAP 24, TARON 13 in Q2 per call; 37 new customers in Q2 per management); about 1,100+ customers total, rising to about 1,300+ with Vimprotech and TIPS.
Third-party logistics pallet penetration up 355% per management, driven by quick-commerce.

qa_highlights.question: Why has receivable days not improved much from March to September, and what is the medium-term outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: DSO fell to 122 days from 128 at start of year; management targets below 90 days by end FY27, citing SAP S/4HANA and needing PO consolidation with about five or six large PO-based customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow cover capex, excluding acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that on an ex-acquisition basis, CFO is adequate for capex; full-year capex about INR450 crore, with possible overshoot if large pallet orders come (e.g. 300,000 pallets).

qa_highlights.question: Why is Vimprotech (manufacturing) being acquired and what benefits are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said in-house moulds and plastics reduce turnaround from about 2 months to about 1 week, protect IP, and could add 600 bps to automotive business and 10-12% margin improvement on plastic crates.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue and PAT will the acquisition add?
qa_highlights.answer: Turnover from November; EBITDA accretive; PAT contribution uncertain due to goodwill. Vimprotech FY26 revenue INR470 mn and TIPS INR180 mn.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the drop in EBITDA margin excluding other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other income is operational (lost equipment charges and sale of broken-beyond-repair components), recurring at 0.5-1.25% of pool value, not interest income; timing varies quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GCC revenue timing and strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue could start as early as next month; management is holding back pricing while evaluating acquisitions in GCC, with decisions expected within one to two quarters; 26 customers engaged.

risks_watch: Granule/plastic price volatility (crude above USD120 cited) hitting textile and automotive demand and crate purchasing costs.
Movement hire ramp must reach 3.6-3.7 million movements in FY27 versus about 720,000 in Q2 and 2.8 million last year; December-March is critical.
Receivables: DSO of 122 days versus target below 90 days by year-end, dependent on PO-based customers.
Vimprotech and TIPS integration, goodwill impact on PAT, and the 50% in-house manufacturing ramp.
GCC go-live timing and pricing, as management is holding prices pending possible acquisitions.
TARON EBITDA margin (about 30%) pulling consolidated margin down; management did not commit to margin recovery to 55-60%.
Lower-than-expected pallet utilisation versus 90-91% target.

544866|2026-06.headline: Molbio Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹408 crore with 25% EBITDA margin and PAT ₹52.7 crore; FY27 guidance ~25% top-line growth.
544866|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹408 crore in Q1 FY27, with 164 devices and 62.4 lakh test kits sold. EBITDA was ₹104 crore (25% margin) and PAT ₹52.7 crore (about 13%). Export revenue was about ₹67 crore (16% of revenue), helped by a catch-up of orders deferred from Q4 FY26 due to Gulf disruption. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 25% and EBITDA margin of 24–25%, while cautioning that quarters are non-linear and OptraScan will not be profitable in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Export ~₹67 crore (16% of revenue), includes catch-up of Q4 FY26 deferrals

financial_highlights.value: Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore; Prognosys ~₹11 crore; OptraScan minimal

financial_highlights.metric: OptraScan loss (Q1 FY27 and comparable 5-month period FY26)

segments.name: Truenat molecular platform (core)
segments.commentary: Kits are about 75% of revenue; installed base ~12,500 machines in 90+ countries, 43 assays across 30 diseases; 40M+ cumulative tests. Gross margin 60–63% across devices and kits per management.

segments.name: Prognosys (70% subsidiary, digital X-ray)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹154 crore and PAT ~₹12 crore; management expects similar ~19% EBITDA margin in FY27. Q1 FY27 revenue ~₹11 crore; US FDA approval for digital imaging and EU MDR for X-ray products.

segments.name: OptraScan (60% subsidiary, digital pathology)
segments.commentary: US FDA clearance received July 2026 for end-to-end workflow incl. software and AI; ~$30 million fresh equity invested. Not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected FY28–FY29.

segments.name: Bigtec Labs (100% R&D subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Bangalore R&D entity with 150+ scientists and 220+ total staff; intercompany kit sales to Bigtec are eliminated on consolidation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at roughly 25%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 24–25%.
Prognosys expected to deliver ~19% EBITDA margin in FY27, similar to FY26.
OptraScan not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected in FY28 and FY29.
Device sales expected in the 2,200–2,600 range for the year, in line with historical levels.
HPV-related revenue timing and volumes to be guided next quarter; R&D to stay at 5–6% of revenue.

Government of India HPV validation led by AIIMS; recommended for national rollout; health technology assessment found it cost-effective for women aged 30–45. Volumes not yet quantified; WHO prequalification application in progress.
Two-year TB rate contract with the government signed last month.
India molecular diagnostics share cited at ~90%; ~8,000–9,000 of an estimated 25,000–30,000 TB diagnostic centres are on Truenat.
Pricing is contract-based, not MRP-led; realisation moves driven by device variant mix (Uno/Duo/Quattro), geography and dollar movements.
Export business started around 2023; distributors in 90 countries; ramp expected to take longer, with EU and US entry being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on the HPV tender and test kit off-take?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals are in place and a recommendation has been made to roll out the test in the national programme; volumes will be clearer by next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the life cycle of a Truenat device and are consumables exclusive?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices have not needed replacement; early 2017–18 installations are still running. The system is closed, so only Molbio cartridges and chips are used; each test consumes one cartridge or chip.

qa_highlights.question: What R&D and capex are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D at 5–6% of revenue; ₹72 crore automation and ~₹105 crore Bangalore R&D centre are the major capex items; no other major capex planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and subsidiary profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore, Prognosys ~₹11 crore, OptraScan minimal. FY26 Prognosys revenue ₹154 crore, PAT ~₹12 crore; OptraScan loss ~₹9 crore in the period.

qa_highlights.question: Is device volume growing and how will the TB/other-disease mix shift?

qa_highlights.question: Is the TB market share sustainable and what is the realisation trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Truenat is the only WHO-endorsed battery-operated point-of-care TB test; remaining centres use microscopy. Pricing is contract-based; realisation moves reflect device mix and FX, with gross margin of 60–63%.

OptraScan loss-making in FY27 and ramp dependent on US lab and hospital adoption after July 2026 FDA clearance.
HPV national-programme volumes and timing not yet quantified; next guidance deferred to next quarter.
Inventory days still high at 230 (trailing 12M), though down from 280 in March.
Export ramp slower than expected; past export volumes have been uneven.
Dependence on public-health TB programme for the bulk of domestic revenue under a two-year rate contract.

So, we will hold this question probably to the next quarter.

rows.label: Two-year TB rate contract with government
rows.why: Signed last month; TB remains the bulk of Truenat test mix (kits ~75% of revenue) and underpins domestic volumes.

rows.label: OptraScan US FDA clearance ramp
rows.why: FDA clearance received July 2026 with ~$30 million fresh equity invested; not profitable in FY27 (~₹9 crore loss in Q1), with meaningful contribution expected FY28-FY29.

544867|2026-06.headline: Dhoot Transmission Q1 FY27: revenue up nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue Rs 1,090 crore (+44.6%), EBITDA margin ~15%; FY27 growth guided at 25-30%.
544867|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong first quarter as its first post-listing call, with growth of nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue up 44.6% and non-wiring harness up 67.7%. EV revenue grew 79% and rose to 27% of total revenue from 24% a year earlier. EBITDA margin improved 110 bps QoQ to about 15%, while raw-material (copper, brass) inflation continued and is being passed through to customers with a roughly three-month lag. Management guided to 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin and 25-30% growth for FY27, while flagging a soft comparison in the first half from last year's GST-driven demand.

financial_highlights.change: Ahead of domestic 2W volumes (>20%) and exports (>36%)
+67.7% YoY vs Rs 213 crore; ~3% of overall growth from Multilink (about 20 days consolidated)
Up from 24% a year ago; EV revenue +79% YoY
Expected to turn to net cash after August IPO proceeds; management indicated ~Rs 1,000 crore net cash around end-August

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,090 crore in Q1 FY27, up 44.6% YoY from Rs 753 crore. Management says localisation has cut imported components from 30-35% to 20-25% of the component base.

segments.name: Non-wiring harness (EV components, battery packs, controllers, sensors, switches)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 358 crore, up 67.7% YoY, with Multilink adding about 10-12 points of that growth. Battery packs are the major portion; a second top customer in the South started supply in the last month of the quarter.

segments.name: Multilink (acquired)
segments.commentary: Contributed ~3% to overall revenue growth for the ~20-day period in Q1. Management expects 25-30% growth and margins in line with the group; full integration in about 3-4 months, adding Hero as a customer plus fuel level sensors and relays.

segments.name: EV vs ICE
segments.commentary: EV revenue +79% YoY, ICE revenue +52.6% YoY. EV content per vehicle is 1.5x-2.5x that of ICE for wiring harness alone, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% YoY, with soft comparison in H1 noted.
Full-year EBITDA margin guided at 15-16%.
Copper and other key raw materials rose further in July and August (~3-4% per management), so gross margin recovery is not expected in Q2; benefit expected in Q3 if prices stay stable.
EV revenue share expected to exceed 30-32% in the next two to three years.
Multilink expected to grow 25-30% at group-level margins after integration in roughly 3-4 months.
Ride Vision (ADAS, Israeli partner) JV formation in process; a passenger-vehicle HV harness JV is at an advanced stage, with details promised in the next earnings call.
IPO proceeds to fund expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur plants, adding ~15-20% capacity this year; IPO utilisation update promised next quarter.
capex_capacity: Expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur plants funded from IPO proceeds, adding ~15-20% to wiring harness capacity this year.
Management says ~75% utilisation is the working ceiling because customers run at full capacity during the 5-6 month Diwali season.
Dhoot Autocomponents (subsidiary) manufactures cables and connection systems, with ~Rs 1,200 crore of business for group companies (self-consumption, not in reported sales).
EV cord set new business for next year: ~40-45% share of the Indian market, per management.
Ride Vision ADAS product: management says it is aimed at two-wheelers first, with regulatory-driven demand expected.
demand_pricing: Management says the EV industry grew ~93% YoY and ICE more than 20% in the quarter, with 2W industry growth of 22.8%.
Copper is ~20-23% of BOM cost. Price pass-through to customers is on a three-month lag; recovery comes when raw materials soften.
Management said the Q1 margin was impacted by a hard commodity cycle, not by mix shift toward battery packs.
Wage-hike cost is recovered from customers through annual discussions, per management.
Management says it has not lost ICE market share, despite an analyst comparison suggesting it had.

qa_highlights.question: How much more margin expansion is possible, and when does copper pass-through normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Kalani said most copper inflation is passed through, but prices kept rising for 4-5 months, so there is some impact. Guidance is kept at 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin; Q2 recovery is unlikely and Q3 is the earliest, if prices are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Cash position and FCF at end-June?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about Rs 220 crore at end-June, after the March Bain infusion and part Multilink impact. Post-IPO money (received in August) should turn the company to net cash, with ~Rs 1,000 crore indicated by end-August.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of non-wiring harness revenue and EBITDA margin expectations for Multilink?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakup by product is not disclosed due to single-customer concentration. Non-wiring harness grew 67.7%, with Multilink adding 10-12 points for its ~20-day contribution. Multilink margins are expected to be in line with group margins.

qa_highlights.question: Wiring harness revenue and prior-year split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: wiring harness Rs 1,090 crore and non-wiring harness Rs 358 crore. Q1 FY26: Rs 753 crore and Rs 213 crore, respectively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity given 75-80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur adds ~15-20% capacity this year. Management said 75% is the sustainable ceiling because of seasonal peak demand during Diwali.

Soft base comparison in H1 FY27, since the GST-cut-driven demand boost came in H2 FY26.

Multilink integration (3-4 months) and cross-selling targets; the Ride Vision JV and passenger-vehicle HV harness JV are not yet finalised.

rows.when: started Q1 FY27 (last month of quarter)

544868|2026-06.headline: Milky Mist Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR973.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9% and gross margin up about 270 bps to 34.2%.
544868|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR973.45 crore, up 44% YoY, led by paneer, cheese, curd, ice cream and yogurt. Gross profit was about INR333 crore (34.2% margin, up ~270 bps), EBITDA INR144.89 crore (14.9% margin vs 12.24% a year earlier) and PAT INR64.67 crore (6.6% margin). Management attributed margin gains to product mix, a ~10.5% price increase taken in Q4 FY26, and scale. The call was the company's first earnings call after listing; several figures were corrected on the call during the prepared remarks.

segments.name: Paneer
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at INR248.29 crore, up 34% in both volume and revenue; management linked this to zero GST on paneer from September 2025 and FSSAI/state bans on analogue paneer. Company claims ~20% share of the organised paneer market.

segments.name: Yogurt (incl. protein range)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR84.5 crore, up 153%; management calls it a key margin driver, with Greek yogurt and Skyr in the protein range.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Volume +45%, revenue +60% YoY, aided by extended summer; management expects demand to stay robust around the year in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

segments.name: Cheese
segments.commentary: Revenue +38% YoY; new natural cheddar plant commissioned in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day capacity. Company says cheese sales come from retail, modern trade and quick-commerce, not QSRs.

segments.name: Curd
segments.commentary: Revenue +27% YoY.

segments.name: Regional mix
segments.commentary: South ~69% of revenue, growing ~44% YoY; non-South ~31%, growing ~50% YoY. Management expects a drift toward 60:40 over time.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to add INR150-200 crore of incremental revenue versus H1 (as stated on the call).
Operating margin: management guided to about 0.5% leverage benefit from scale; asked whether 18% EBITDA margin is achievable in 3-4 years, CFO said 'you can expect that' but CEO declined to quantify.
Maharashtra plant: at drawing-board stage, about three years out; the company aims for 40% utilisation from day one at break-even.
Revenue potential from Perundurai at current MRP: 3x to 3.5x FY26 revenue (as stated on the call).
Plans to deploy more than 50,000 visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers over the next three fiscal years.
Whey protein concentrate plant expected to be operational in about 15-18 months from the call.
capex_capacity: Commissioned new natural cheddar cheese plant in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day installed capacity.

Capex in the RHP: about INR500 crore plus INR150 crore, about INR650-700 crore in total; another ~INR380 crore WIP carried from last year. CFO said capex is funded through IPO proceeds and bank funding, with no cash-flow pressure this year.
Planned expansion covers whey protein concentrate, lactose, natural cheese, processed cheese and yogurt capacity.
Capacity utilisation: CEO said more than 12 product categories have spare capacity; paneer utilisation is about 50%.

Milk procurement averaged 13.2 lakh litres per day in Q1 FY27, up 28% YoY. Third-party share is about 10-12% of volume, and the company is expanding direct procurement in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 10.5% taken in Q4 FY26 (stated as ~11% in one answer); management said this offset milk and input inflation and produced a 2.7% margin expansion net.
Trade spend: about 4.5-5% trade discount from MRP to billing and another 4.5-5% on marketing/promotion.
Milk costs are about 50-55% of input cost; landed cost is INR45/litre (farmer price INR41-42). Aavin raised farmgate prices by INR3 twice recently; management is still studying pass-through.
Pricing is set after a 2-3 month lag following input cost increases, per CFO.
Management said the company has no B2B or QSR sales other than whey powder from cheese and paneer making.

qa_highlights.question: Third-party milk procurement strategy and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party share is about 10-12% through a five-year exclusive contract with MilkLane (linked to a PE-owned entity). Management says payments go directly to farmers and that quality premiums are about 50 paise/litre, with no financial dilution.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin resilience amid milk price inflation and further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credits product mix (paneer +34%, cheese +38%, yogurt +150%, ice cream +60%) and pricing. Price hikes follow a 2-3 month lag after input costs. About 10.5% price increase taken last year.

qa_highlights.question: Freight and logistics model with a single plant serving distant cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-owned fleet of about 375 vehicles with return-load logistics saves ~18-20% on logistics cost. Shelf life of 30+ days (vs 24-48 hours for pouch milk) makes one plant viable.

qa_highlights.question: Low base in Q1 FY26 and seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 weakness was price-driven (GST and milk rationalisation), not volume-driven. Ice cream is strong in summer and robust year-round in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

qa_highlights.question: Whey protein plans and high-protein B2C products?
qa_highlights.answer: The company generates about 1 million litres of cheese whey daily and currently sells whey powder B2B. A whey protein concentrate plant is due in 15-18 months; high-protein RTD products are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Yield per animal and farmer support?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement volume is up 28% YoY. Initiatives include bank credit via Kisan Credit Cards, herd-size expansion, AI/breeding, feed and health camps.

risks_watch: Milk procurement cost inflation: Aavin raised farmgate prices by INR3 twice recently and a report cites Tamil Nadu procurement price hikes of around 15%; management is still studying pass-through and has not confirmed price action beyond the 10.5% taken in Q4 FY26.

Third-party milk share (~10-12%, via MilkLane under a five-year exclusive contract linked to a PE-owned entity): watch whether this share falls as direct procurement expands in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra, and any impact on quality costs.

Paneer growth dependence on zero GST from September 2025 and state/FSSAI analogue paneer bans; the price gap between organised and unorganised players is now near nil, so volume gains depend on enforcement continuing.

544870|2026-06.headline: Behari Lal Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR29.7 crore (19.6% margin) and high-value share at 60.4%.
544870|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's first earnings call as a listed entity, following its IPO (INR301 crore issue, listed 19 August 2026). Management guided to about INR80 crore of FY27 capex, with Unit 3 (centrifugal/foundry for ICDP and HSS rolls) targeted to start in Q1 FY28, while defense revenue is expected to become meaningful from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?

segments.commentary: INR29.7 crores in Q1 FY27, up 17% YoY; LTM INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains and INR20 crores carry per the LTM split given on the call). Carry is booked on a realised basis only. Q1 carry of INR13 crores came from Fund II.

guidance_outlook: Management has a stated policy of not giving future guidance on carry, fund wind-up, deployment or fundraising timelines.
Fund V (flagship) targets INR2,500 crores over a 10-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received. Management said the size may increase a bit.
Eastgate (secondaries) targets INR1,500 crores over a 5-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received.
Historical trendlines cited: profit about 35% CAGR (Mar-24 to Mar-26) and total income about 24% a year. Not presented as guidance.
Dividend of INR0.75 per share (15%); payout ratio raised to 12.5% from about 10%.
PW (PricewaterhouseCoopers) to be appointed statutory auditor, replacing the previous auditor.
capex_capacity: Fund V (flagship): seeking INR2,500 crores over a 10-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received; management said size may increase a bit; targets 10-12 investments; enterprise values up to INR2,000 crores with scale potential to INR10,000 crores.
Eastgate (secondaries): seeking INR1,500 crores over a 5-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received; provides liquidity to Indian PE/VC managers via portfolio stake acquisitions.
Fund IV: closed 2023 at INR1,775 crores across 7 investments; 75% deployed at 30 June 2026, rising to 81% after one further call; gross IRR 29%, gross MOIC 1.8x.
Fee-paying initial committed capital of Funds III and IV is roughly INR3,200 crores; management said fee income does not grow with NAV.
Management said the two new funds (Fund V and Eastgate) are proposed for launch in FY26-27 and declined to give timelines for wind-up, deployment or first close.
demand_pricing: Fund IV (closed 2023, INR1,775 crores, 7 investments): 75% deployed at 30 June 2026, now 81% after one more investment; gross IRR 29%, gross MOIC 1.8x.
Fund III gross IRR cited at about 9% (analyst figure, from CRISIL cohort data); management says it already earns sponsor gains from Fund III.
Sponsor commitment across funds about INR589 crores, 7.1% of fund size.
Investor base: 298 LPs in existing funds; about 900 investors across India and 20+ countries; little reliance on distributors.
Hurdle rates: 10% for rupee investors, 8% for dollar investors; European (whole-fund) waterfall with full catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: Fund IV dry powder and number of targeted investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 10-12 investments per fund; seven made in Fund IV by June 2026, deployment at 75% rising to 81% since. Fund V will also target 10-12 investments.

qa_highlights.question: Share of carry vs fee income and whether pure fee income will grow faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said performance income becomes more predictable as firms mature, and that fee income does not grow with NAV. Q1 split was about INR16 crores fee and INR30 crores performance; LTM is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of performance income into carry and sponsor gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: INR13 crores carry from Fund II and INR17 crores sponsor gains from Funds III and IV, total INR29.7 crores. LTM performance income INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains, INR20 crores carry). Carry is booked on realised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Fund III carry given low gross IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to say; NAVs are carried conservatively and it expects Fund III performance income trends to continue, with sponsor gains already flowing.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 to Q1 jump of about 594% in carry fee; is it realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 FY26 weakness to low markets and multiple re-rating in March 2026. The Q1 jump reflects fair value gains from the recovery in markets through June, not realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to AI deals such as Fractal and Sarvam and entry valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to discuss underlying fund investments in detail. Said both are mature growth-stage deals, not venture; sector exposure capped at 20-25% of fund capital.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost rise from Q4 to Q1 (INR6.7 crores to INR10.3 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 has seasonal bonus payouts; YoY, Q1 employee costs are in the same range of INR10-plus crores.

qa_highlights.question: Market value of portfolio and LP share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no single portfolio; valuations are done quarterly under SEBI rules and the same valuations are used for the company's holdings.

qa_highlights.question: Fund III and Fund V, Eastgate timelines and first closes?
qa_highlights.answer: Declined to give future guidance on wind-up, deployment or fundraising timing.

risks_watch: Performance income is lumpy quarter to quarter (Q4 FY26 carry sharply lower, Q1 FY27 up about 594% QoQ); management asks investors to judge on LTM.
Fund III gross IRR of about 9% is well below the 10% rupee hurdle and carry depends on returning capital plus hurdle; no carry guidance given.
Carry is booked only on realisations, so timing of fund exits will drive reported earnings.
Fund IV valuation and AI-sector exposure (Fractal, Sarvam) questioned by analysts; management declined detailed disclosure.
Auditor change to PW and fundraising for Fund V (INR2,500 crores) and Eastgate (INR1,500 crores) are pending milestones.

Management repeatedly declined guidance on carry, deployment, fund-raise timing and Fund III outcome, citing board and adviser advice. Explanations of quarterly variance leaned on LTM framing.

544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.
544886|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 33% YoY to INR118 crores, led by Electrical Heating (+148.8% to INR25 crores) and Temperature Sensing (+42% to INR60 crores), while Specialized Cables fell 8.8% to INR32.5 crores on export order timing. EBITDA rose 15.7% to INR26.6 crores, but margin compressed about 330 bps to 22%, driven by a roughly 140 bps hit from employee cost (up 45% to INR20.4 crores) and a high prior-year gross margin base. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in line with the three-year blended growth rate and said margins should recover in H2 FY27. Four capacity projects with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores are slated to commission between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Temperature Sensing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR60 crores, up 42%, led by thermal power and OEMs including CVD equipment makers; EDGE pyrometer series (with Micro-Epsilon) to start dispatch in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Electrical Heating
segments.commentary: Revenue INR25 crores, up 148.8% on oil and gas dispatches in India, Southeast Asia and Middle East; 5-year standard furnace supply contract signed with a life sciences OEM.

segments.name: Specialized Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crores, down 8.8% on export order timing; cable harness line launched with UL certification; Unit 8 greenfield under construction, completion by Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected in line with blended three-year growth; management pointed to about 25% in analyst's framing but said visibility improves in H2.
EBITDA margin to remain broadly similar to FY26 profile; margin recovery visible in H2 FY27 as employee cost is absorbed by revenue.
Management expects profit growth to be in line with revenue growth by end of FY27.
Lower finance cost to be visible from the coming quarter after INR55 crores of IPO proceeds used for debt repayment.
OEM and new products expected to contribute more than 25% of revenue starting FY28.
capex_capacity: Brownfield 50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 1 for OEM contact sensors, commissioning by Q3 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 6 for medium-voltage heaters, completion by Q1 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR200 crores; heaters tested to 7.2 kV, explosion-proof certification targeted by Q4 FY27.
Unit 8 greenfield cable plant, completion by Q2 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR60 crores; capacity can be ramped quickly.
Victura JV to acquire 80,000 sq ft facility with existing shed; production to start by Q4 FY27, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

Aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores across four projects versus FY26 revenue of INR445 crores; existing capacity running at about 80%. Additional 25,000 sq ft planned for custom furnaces this year; land acquired for about INR25 crores in Q1 for cable expansion.
demand_pricing: Pipeline healthy across thermal and nuclear power in India and steel and glass globally; quoted pipeline in Middle East has increased but firm orders still awaited.
OEM order visibility of 9-12 months versus about 4-4.5 months order book for heavy-industry customers; furnace contract is 5 years.
Inventory of INR110-120 crores, 65-70% in raw material; raw materials booked at order receipt and price fluctuations passed through to customers.
Management says Chinese competition is limited for engineered make-to-order products; some customers shifting sourcing to India.
Export share rose to about 34%; new subsidiaries in Mexico, Poland and South Korea; Korean JV supplying battery manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: How has the fuel cell OEM order trajectory evolved and what run-rate exit FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said field trials and run-up are advanced and focus is now on scaling execution; it declined to quantify exit run-rate, calling it a work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from critical, high-barrier industries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated roughly 75-90% of revenue from critical applications, with 10-20% from regular, more competitive industries; vendor approvals can take 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the new-age industry TAM and its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify TAM; said new-age products could grow in the high 20s or 30s percent over 2-3 years. Newer products segment addressable market is about INR3,000 crores with less than 1% currently addressed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin recovery bridge and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost increase reflects headcount added for future projects; margin recovery expected to start in H2 FY27, not FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East/Africa and political situation a risk to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no negative impact seen in the next few quarters; electrification trend could be positive mid-term.

qa_highlights.question: When will the INR500 crore incremental capacity reach full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity comes online from Q1 FY28 with construction largely done by Q3 FY28; full utilisation expected around FY29-FY30, with plants typically run at about 80% maximum.

financial_highlights.change: +148.8% YoY, low base as heater facility commissioned end of Q1 FY26
+45% YoY, about 140 bps margin impact; includes INR57 lakh ESOP charge in prior-year quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (excl. amortisation of acquisition and intangibles)

risks_watch: Margin recovery hinges on H2 FY27: management says employee cost will be absorbed by revenue, and the EBITDA margin was 22% in Q1 versus 25.3% a year earlier.
Execution of about INR500 crores of peak capacity across four projects (Q4 FY27 to Q3 FY28); management said full utilisation may take until FY29-FY30, and the Victura JV facility starts by Q4 FY27.
Fuel cell OEM ramp: management declined to quantify the exit FY27 run-rate or order book size, calling it a work in progress.

Q1 export timing: Specialized Cables fell 8.8% on export order timing, and the Electrical Heating base effect (+148.8%) will fade from Q2 FY27 onward.

Inventory of INR110-120 crores with 65-70% in raw material; the company books raw materials at order receipt and passes through price fluctuations, which needs monitoring if input prices move sharply.
key_quotes: So, we have not really differentiate on the margin profile on the different segments, but the blended margin is already available with you.
This is like a work in progress, and we will come back with the exact results as we execute these projects.
We have not seen any impact as of now, but I think in mid- midterm, it will be a positive thing for the company.
So, we are adding in capacities, I mean, which will be online by Q3 FY28 of about INR500 crores of additional revenue.

It framed the Q1 margin decline as deliberate investment ahead of projects, with recovery promised for H2 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: EDGE pyrometer series with Micro-Epsilon starts dispatch in Q3 FY27, the cable harness line with UL certification has launched, and heater explosion-proof certification is targeted by Q4 FY27 for the 7.2 kV range.

rows.label: OEM order visibility 9-12 months and 5-year furnace contract
rows.why: OEM order visibility is 9-12 months versus a 4-4.5 month heavy-industry order book, and a 5-year standard furnace supply contract was signed with a life sciences OEM.

rows.why: Export share rose to about 34% of revenue (INR39.8 cr, +78.3%), new subsidiaries were set up in Mexico, Poland and South Korea, and the Korean JV is supplying battery manufacturers.

rows.label: Lower finance cost from IPO-funded debt repayment
rows.why: INR55 cr of IPO proceeds were used for debt repayment, and management says lower finance cost will be visible from the coming quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, exports, the pipeline and the INR500 cr capacity plan, but cautious on margins and evasive on quantification, declining to give the fuel cell exit run-rate, order book size, TAM or Middle East timing; analysts pushed on the H2 margin recovery and fuel cell ramp.

544889|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR218 crores, while new-business opex drag of INR23 crores left consolidated EBITDA at INR45 crores.
544889|2026-06.overview: Symbiotec's first earnings call after its BSE/NSE listing reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR218 crores (+7% YoY), with API revenue of INR215 crores (+6% YoY, volume-led) and API EBITDA of INR66 crores (+9% YoY). Consolidated EBITDA was INR45 crores and net profit about INR14 crores, which management said understates underlying profitability because of INR23 crores of new-business opex and INR11 crores of depreciation that were previously capitalised as pre-operative expenses. No CDMO or injectable revenue was booked in the quarter, versus about INR33 crores of milestone revenue in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of roughly 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus/minus 5% band, and pinned new-business revenue to milestones in H2 FY27 and commercial CDMO revenue to the next 6 to 12 months.

financial_highlights.change: About INR326 crores after IPO proceeds of INR142 crores and September-quarter capex

segments.name: API (steroid and hormone APIs)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR215 crores, +6% YoY, driven largely by volume; API EBITDA INR66 crores, +9% YoY; gross margin 60%+. Management says more than 90% of FY27 revenue comes from API. Capacity utilisation is about 70-80%.

segments.name: Biotech CDMO (fermentation)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27. Built on about 400 kL of large-scale fermentation at Ujjain, with signed 10-year take-or-pay with a US alternate-protein player and 5-year take-or-pay for insulin drug substance. Small revenues are guided for Q4 FY27 and meaningful revenues for FY28.

segments.name: Complex injectables (dual-chamber vials/bags)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27 (Q4 FY26 had about INR33 crores of milestone revenue across CDMO and injectables). First DCV ANDA filed in September 2026; second molecule ANDA planned for Q4 FY27. Term sheet with a large US pharma multinational; definitive agreement expected early Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% and EBITDA growth of about 25% on a consolidated basis, with a plus/minus 5% band citing global operating uncertainty.
PAT growth will be lower than EBITDA growth because of depreciation drag; cash PAT (PAT plus depreciation) growth is expected to be above 25%.
New-business opex of about INR23 crores and depreciation of about INR11 crores per quarter to run for the next two to three quarters.
Management expects the first couple of quarters to be lumpy, with a strong H2 FY27 from milestone cash flows (Q3/Q4) that management says will offset the new-business opex.
Insulin/biologics revenue expected to start early FY28, pending stability studies and DCGI approval.
Capex of INR200-250 crores per year for the next two to three years, funded by internal accruals and customer contributions.
capex_capacity: Cumulative investment of more than INR1,000 crores in the two new businesses, of which over INR500 crores is in biomanufacturing/biopharma fermentation.
Gross block in API about INR640 crores as of 30 June 2026; management cites INR800-900 crores of API revenue and asset turnover of about 1.5x.

Phase 0: existing 400 kL fermentation capacity, largely booked under current contracts. Phase 1: brownfield expansion of about 600 kL (about 4x the current capacity) with construction starting Q3 FY27 and 15-18 months to build.
DCV: five to six products developed and moving to plant-level validation; a second DCV line may be needed soon due to capacity constraints.
Mhow injectable facility is part of the roughly INR1,000 crores invested in new businesses.
demand_pricing: Management says demand and traction are very strong, with discussions with more than half a dozen potential customers, each seeking about 1 million litres of fermentation capacity.
Take-or-pay contracts are multi-million-dollar per customer; management declined to disclose per-litre pricing, minimum revenue or contract values, citing confidentiality.
Management guides to industry-level margins for complex injectables and CDMO: gross margin above 70% and EBITDA margin above 35%, and expects Symbiotec to be in a similar range.

API gross margin guided at around 60% (currently above 60%), with EBITDA margin near 30%. Management attributes margin strength to backward integration (make vs buy) and mix shift toward regulated markets.
Customer base: over 200 customers in more than 40 countries; about 70% of FY26 revenue from customers served for more than seven years.

qa_highlights.question: How should capacity, revenue and take-or-pay minimums in the fermentation business be framed over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the advanced-stage contracts would require about four times the current capacity (Phase 1, over 2-3 years). It did not give per-litre revenue or minimum revenue numbers, only that each contract is multi-million dollar and asset turnover should exceed 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 600 kL expansion for existing or new customers, and what is the capex?
qa_highlights.answer: The 600 kL Phase 1 is tied to a customer with a signed term sheet, with construction starting Q3 FY27 and taking 15-18 months. Funding combines internal accruals with customer contributions; no specific outlay was given beyond INR200-250 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: What are opex and milestone expectations for the new businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR23 crores quarterly opex run rate should continue for two to three quarters. Management said H2 milestone revenues would offset the full-year new-business opex, without giving amounts.

qa_highlights.question: How long before DCV launches, and how many products follow?
qa_highlights.answer: The first DCV ANDA is filed, the second is due in Q4 FY27, and five to six products are in development. Management said capacity, not product count, is the constraint, and a second line may be needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no revenue from CDMO and injectables in Q1, and what were last year's milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Milestone revenue is periodic, not quarterly. About INR33 crores was recognised in Q4 FY26, and none in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is API capacity utilisation and gross and EBITDA margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: API utilisation is about 70-80%. Management expects gross margin around 60% and EBITDA margin near 30%, with variance from logistics and solvent prices.

qa_highlights.question: Premarin generic timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give timing, saying the partner controls formulation development and FDA submission; Symbiotec's part is the API.

qa_highlights.question: API share of revenue two years out?
qa_highlights.answer: API is over 90% of revenue today. Management expects it to fall below half in 5-6 years as CDMO and DCV scale.

risks_watch: Milestone-driven H2 FY27 revenue: management says Q3/Q4 milestones will offset roughly INR23 crores per quarter of new-business opex, but gave no amounts; watch whether the definitive DCV agreement with the US multinational is signed in early Q3 FY27.
Regulatory timing: US FDA audit at Pithampur completed August 2026 with procedural observations under response, EIR awaited; first DCV ANDA filed September 2026, second planned for Q4 FY27.
Biologics/insulin revenue slipping to early FY28 pending stability studies and DCGI approval; CDMO revenue guided small in Q4 FY27 and meaningful in FY28.

And on the commercial note on dual chamber vial platform, in August 2026, we signed a term sheet with a very large US-based pharmaceutical multinational covering products from this platform.
So, I don't see any reason why would this profile change.

544891|2026-06.headline: Hy-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR430 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 19.6% from 21.5%, which management blames on price-revision timing.
544891|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR430 million and PAT rose 11% to INR46 million, while EBITDA was flat at INR84 million and margin contracted about 190 bps. Management attributed the margin dip to input-cost increases from the Feb–April period whose OEM price revisions, effective 1 April, are expected to be recognised only in Q2, and a cut-off sales shift into the next quarter. This was the company's first earnings call after its 1 September listing on NSE and BSE. Management guided to ~20% revenue growth, 25–30% PAT growth and a 24–25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with capacity expansion and new-customer wins as the main drivers.

rows.why: The Sharon AI go-live has already slipped from mid-September to early November and billing timelines differ (Q3 FY27 vs Q1 FY28), so further slippage is a real risk.

rows.label: Sharon AI 7-year GPU lease with locked pricing
rows.when: Billing from Q3 FY27 (early Nov go-live)
rows.why: 8,200 B300 GPUs in Sydney under a 7-year lease with purchase cost and customer revenue both locked; customers pay 12 to 18 months advance internationally.

rows.label: Target GPU lease pricing USD 5 to 6 per GPU hour
rows.why: Management targets USD 5 to 6 per GPU hour for own capacity and will lease when prices rise around January, but is not yet signing customers for the new India capacity.

rows.label: Customer advances funding GPU capex
rows.why: Customer advances of about INR 1,177 crore fund part of capex, and Sharon AI now demands 50% advance per management.

tone.note: Management was confident on GPU demand (50,000+ GPU funnel), locked B300 pricing and PAT margin targets of 15-20%, but cautious and vague on timelines, shifting the Sharon AI go-live repeatedly and declining FY27/FY28 guidance; analysts pressed on the 7-8% revenue growth versus 30-40% order book CAG

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow (INR19 crores) and rising borrowings (INR436 crores at June 2026 vs INR371 crores at FY26 end) despite lower inventory and working capital; management has not given a self-funding date.

Cost base from four new large-format centres is largely fixed: Q1 cost structure is expected to carry into Q2, and no significant expansion is planned near term. EBITDA break-even needs about INR55 crores of gross profit (INR45 crores lease-related costs on P&L basis; INR29 crores on cash basis).

Customer advances (INR49 crores, about one month of revenue) support working capital; the reduction in net working capital partly reflects these advances, so the trend depends on backorder volumes continuing.

New York store (opened March 2026) has only about three months of operating data; break-even GMV not given; June-end lease with shorter tenure allows rent adjustment after 12-18 months of performance.

No store-level or same-store sales disclosure; geography-level reporting makes it hard to isolate store productivity. US GMV fell to INR77 crores in FY26 from INR136-138 crores in FY24 (per an analyst), as the long tail was trimmed and the US was online-only until March 2026.
Consignment share of inventory is not disclosed; management called it business-sensitive, limiting visibility on inventory mix and risk.
Management said it would refrain from objective margin or profitability guidance; the next two quarters are the stated point for clearer trends.
key_quotes: So the operating leverage which is delivered in the business because of the fixed cash flow usually reflects in the subsequent quarters of the business.
Honestly, any objective guidance at this point, we would refrain from.
So which means on a cash basis, on that you will have to add another INR29 crores GP to become EBITDA positive.
Now on the consignment bit, I think that's a business-sensitive data, so that I'll not be able to disclose publicly.
544901|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the strategy and the fixed-cost framing, but cautious and repeatedly deferring on profitability, cash flow and working capital, asking investors to observe the next two quarters. Evasive on consignment split and on store-level or same-store metrics, citing business sensitivity or the geography-based reporting model.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.why: Four large-format centres opened in FY26 are already operating and management says no significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of store investment is to be observed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores (+45% YoY) and revenue to INR119 crores from INR106 crores (+12%), driven by AOV up to INR86,000 from INR66,000 and the first full quarter of four new stores; growth is in ticket size more than unit count.
