rows.why: Cost base from new stores is largely fixed and Q1 cost structure carries into Q2; borrowings rose to INR436 crores from INR371 crores and operating cash burn is INR19 crores, so profitability and cash trends could disappoint.

rows.label: Borrowings rising, self-funding date not given
rows.why: Borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end while operating cash flow was -INR19 crores; management gave no self-funding date and only said finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

rows.label: New York flagship ramp and lease reset
rows.why: New York store opened March 2026 with about three months of data, estimated AOV about INR1.25 lakh; the June-end lease has a shorter tenure allowing rent adjustment after 12-18 months, but no break-even GMV was given.

rows.label: Customer advances supporting working capital
rows.why: Customer advances rose to INR49 crores from INR37 crores (+32% YoY) and NWC fell to INR66 crores from INR105 crores, but this depends on backorder volumes continuing, and backorder advances are about one month of revenue.

544903|2026-09.headline: Deepa Jewellers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.24% on plain-gold mix and PAT rose 37% to INR 37 crore.
544903|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (up 17% YoY, margin 7.24%) and PAT of INR 37 crore (up 37%, margin 5.96%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,057 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to INR 84 crore (7.95% margin) and PAT rose 32% to INR 64 crore. Management attributed the Q2 growth moderation to festive demand shifting into H2, and said lower gross margin came from a plain-gold-heavy sales mix, with PAT supported by other income and a lower tax rate. The company also commenced its in-house Hyderabad manufacturing facility in September 2026 and guided to 40-45% revenue CAGR for FY27-FY29.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Volume of 318 kg in Q2 (+44% YoY) and 544 kg in H1 (+51% YoY). Realisation per gram fell to about INR 178-180 from about INR 200 a year earlier, which management attributed to plain-gold mix rather than pricing changes.

segments.name: Jewellery manufacturing (invoice/own gold)
segments.commentary: Volume of 491 kg in Q2 (broadly stable) and 783 kg in H1 (-5% YoY). Own-processing realisation fell to about INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g, attributed to lower gold prices, plain-gold mix and higher 18-karat sales.

segments.name: Studded vs plain gold mix
segments.commentary: Studded share was 57% of H1 FY27 sales, against 65% in FY26, with plain gold at 43%. Management targets studded share of 75% over the next three to four quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% guided for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with FY27 growth of 40-45% compared with FY26 (March 2026) base; the 40-45% figure was also described as a 40-50% revenue CAGR for two years at a constant 24-karat gold rate of INR 50,000.
EBITDA margin expected to expand 80-120 bps over the next 4-6 quarters, driven by the Hyderabad facility, Tier-2/3 expansion, studded mix and standalone store sales.
Gross margin pressure from plain-gold mix expected to normalise in upcoming quarters.
Hedging to rise from 94% toward close to 100% of gold holdings over the next two to three quarters.
Working capital cycle (inventory days plus receivable days) expected in the 55-65 day range; inventory and receivables expected to normalise from Q3.
Internal accruals, IPO proceeds and existing debt expected to fund growth through FY29.
Effective tax rate guided at the standard 25.168%; Q2 benefit came from deferred tax on IPO expenses, with the tax shield reversing in later years.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad, about 6,700 sq ft, commenced operations in September 2026.
Facility capacity of about 1.5 tonnes a year on single shift and about 2.5 tonnes a year on double shift.
Facility processed 65 kg (13% of volume) in Q1 FY27 and 167 kg (21%) in Q2 FY27; management expects about 40% in Q3 and about 50% in Q4.
Second sales office in Chennai planned for December 2026; Bangalore office planned for April-May 2027, following Vijayawada office.
Long-run target mix of 65% in-house and 35% outsourced manufacturing; outsourced work to shift in-house from Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Revenue concentrated in South India (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala); client base about 373 customers including 47 jewellery retail chains such as Joyalukkas, Kalyan, Lalitha and Bhima.
Q2 growth moderated as festive demand shifted into H2; H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue.
Retail customers shifting from cash purchases to old-gold exchange after a gold price spike, moving sales from invoice basis to job work; management said total volume shifted rather than fell.

Job work conversion margin is about 75% and invoice-basis about 8%, with a similar ROCE/ROE in both models; job work is priced at about 1% lower wastage (4% vs 5%) because it needs no working capital.
Gold price assumption for guidance: constant 24-karat rate of INR 50,000 per 10 g; average selling gold price rose from about INR 8,000/g in FY25 to INR 11,950/g in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin and grammage realisation decline in Q2, and why did job work realisation drop about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change was a shift toward plain gold jewellery (lower margin than studded), not a strategic or operational change, and expects normalisation. Job work realisation fell to about INR 178 from INR 202 a year earlier (about 11%), attributed to the same SKU mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and receivable days rise versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March is not a like-for-like base because year-end corporate purchases stop; higher inventory came from stock built for the new Vijayawada sales office in September after IPO proceeds. Management expects normalisation from Q3 and a combined inventory plus receivable cycle of 55-65 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from new geographies (Vijayawada, Chennai, Bangalore offices), SKU expansion into studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery (16 SKUs launched in Q1), and client store expansion including franchise models. Guidance is 40-45% CAGR for FY27-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the new facility, and what EBITDA margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation and karigar costs weighed on Q1 and Q2 margins; benefit expected from Q3 as more volume shifts in-house. Management guided to an 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters, with a note that studded mix and standalone store sales also contribute.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price exposure hedged, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: 94% of gold holdings were hedged as of 30 September through gold metal loans (3.25% p.a.), MCX short futures and back-to-back unfixed purchases from bullion suppliers. Target is close to 100% within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to about 15%, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the standard rate is 25.168%; the lower Q2 rate reflects deferred tax on IPO expenses, which Companies Act treats against securities premium while Income Tax allows over five years. The effect is expected to even out in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters draw salary, and how will they be compensated?
qa_highlights.answer: Both Ashish Agarwal and Dev Agarwal will not draw salary from 1 October 2026, and Dev Agarwal said no salary is planned for at least 10 quarters, after which the board will decide.

risks_watch: Gross margin and realisation pressure from plain-gold mix and lower gold prices; management quantified a 50% gold price fall at about 60 bps gross margin impact.
Working capital intensity: inventory and receivable days rose versus September FY26, and growth of 40-45% needs funding from accruals, IPO proceeds and debt.
Execution risk on new Hyderabad plant ramp-up (targeted about 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4) and on Chennai and Bangalore office launches.
Shift of retail customers toward old-gold exchange could keep invoice-basis sales subdued and raise job work share.
Customer concentration in South India and in a few large jewellery chains.
Tax rate normalisation from Q2 deferred benefit back to 25.168%.
Hedging coverage to rise to close to 100%; monitor in next quarter.
544903|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin recovery, with management repeatedly describing Q2 softness as a mix and timing effect. Management was more evasive on specifics, notably the EBITDA margin direction (a live misstatement of 80-120 bps versus a dip was clarified on the call) and on the basis for the 40-45% CAGR. Answers on the old-gold shift and inventory build were detailed and conceded the points.
key_quotes: So, from the 3rd Quarter onwards, both the promoters will not be drawing any salary from the business.
It is just a change in the SKU mix which is expected to normalize in the upcoming quarters.
But yes, I accept that there has been a slight increase in the inventory days as well as the trade receivable days when we compare it to the numbers of September Fiscal '26.
So, over the next 4-5 quarters, we expect about 80-120 bps increase in our EBITDA margins over a period of next 4-6 quarters.
Sir, it is not a dip sir, I mentioned that our EBITDA margin will increase by 80 to 120 basis points.

As of now, I as promoter of the company on a personal front have sufficient liquidity and as we are more inclined to the faster growth of the company, currently we have no plans of drawing any kind of salary at least for 10 quarters from now.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters from Hyderabad in-house shift, Tier-2/3 expansion and studded mix (57% of H1 sales vs 65% FY26, target 75% in 3-4 quarters), but Q2 margin fell to 7.24% and H1 margin is 7.95%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward (Chennai Dec 2026, Bangalore Apr-May 2027)
rows.why: Hyderabad facility commenced Sept 2026 (1.5 t/yr single shift, 2.5 t/yr double shift), with in-house share targeted at 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4 from 21% in Q2; Chennai office dated Dec 2026 and Bangalore Apr-May 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Total operating volume grew 13% YoY to 809 kg in Q2 and 12% to 1,327 kg in H1, with job work up 44% in Q2; processing/manufacturing was flat (-5% in H1), and festive demand is expected in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed; the single-shift Hyderabad plant has 1.5 t/yr capacity with 167 kg processed in Q2, and the company plans a 65% in-house target, so further capacity could be needed, but no new capex was guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue growth slowed to 25% YoY from H1's 30%, and the 40-45% CAGR is not tied to specific orders, so there is no sign of a guidance raise yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth decelerated from 30% in H1 to 25% in Q2, the Hyderabad ramp (21% to 50% of volume by Q4) and working capital (55-65 day cycle) are execution risks, and the 40-45% CAGR is not backed by specific orders.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery SKUs were launched (16 SKUs in Q1), and management cited SKU expansion as a growth driver, but no specific new launch dates were given beyond those.

rows.label: Inventory plus receivable cycle back to 55-65 days
rows.why: Management said inventory and receivables will normalise from Q3 and expects a combined cycle of 55-65 days, with higher inventory tied to stock built for the Vijayawada office after IPO proceeds.

rows.label: Gold hedging rising to near 100%
rows.why: Hedging rose to 94% of gold holdings at 30 September from 75% over 2-3 years, with a stated aim of close to 100% in 2-3 quarters, which cuts price risk.

rows.label: Gross margin normalisation from plain-gold mix
rows.why: Job work realisation fell to about INR 178/g from about INR 200/g and own-processing to INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g; management expects normalisation, but a 50% gold price fall would cut gross margin about 60 bps.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 40-45% CAGR, the Hyderabad ramp and margin recovery, and described Q2 softness as mix and timing; analysts pressed on the margin direction, the basis for the CAGR, the low tax rate, and the inventory build.

544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR950 crore with EBITDA margin similar to FY26, with H2 as the main execution period.

financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.name: By end-user
segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.name: Voltage mix (other)
segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR950 crore, with EBITDA margin broadly similar to FY26.
FY28 revenue growth expected to be similar to FY27 guidance (about 40-45% per analyst's read, not confirmed by management).
Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.
Order book at end-FY27 may be adequate to cover FY28 and FY29 revenue, per management; no specific FY27 closing order book number given.
Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity about 19,200 MVA across Rithani and Gangol (Meerut); Gangol about 18,000 MVA.
Q1 FY27 executed about 1,725 MVA, implying roughly 36-46% utilisation depending on base used.
Planned brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol; part funded from IPO proceeds.
765 kV: technology developed in-house; capacity to be suitable for 765 kV; management estimates 3-4 years to become eligible for regular 765 kV tenders.
About 2,500 kW solar plant planned, partly funded from IPO proceeds; savings not quantified.
demand_pricing: Management estimates India 400 kV transformer market at about 60,000-70,000 MVA last year, growing 10-15% industry-wide; analyst's INR4,000-6,000 crore 400 kV market size was confirmed as 'in that range'.
Railways envisages about 1,000 traction substations for high-speed rail over 5-10 years (about 2,000 transformers), implying about INR20,000 crore opportunity.
Most contracts have price variation clauses (IEEMA PVC), which management says offsets raw material swings; order book margins said to be similar to FY26.
Industry lead times are 18-24 months; tenders being bid are mainly for FY29-FY30 execution.
Revenue per MVA about INR6.1 lakh last year; may have risen slightly due to raw material costs.
Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY24 focus went to obtaining 400 kV and Scott certifications; ramp-up takes time. Exports are not the current focus; a re-look may come in 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Supply chain and raw material availability, which management named as the key risk; geopolitical sourcing issues were raised.
Margin pressure from new 400 kV entrants and added capacity beyond the 3-4 year visibility window.
Execution timing: H2-weighted revenue and 18-24 month execution cycles.
Capacity addition: brownfield 18,000 MVA must come on stream by FY28-FY29 to support growth.
Order book lumpiness toward power transformers, with large CPSU orders (INR250 crore+) in Q2.
Working capital intensity of 110-120 net days.
Management did not disclose bid pipeline, EBITDA by segment, or the MVA-based breakdown beyond Q1 execution.

544921|2026-06.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.

AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. Consolidated PAT was INR59 crores versus standalone INR143 crores, and management urged investors to assess the company on a standalone and full-year basis.

544949|2026-09.headline: Swastika Infra H1 FY27 revenue INR207 crores (+5% YoY), Q2 revenue +42% to INR188 crores; unexecuted order book about INR1,420 crores.
544949|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's maiden analyst call after listing on NSE and BSE. Q2 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR188 crores, EBITDA 62% to INR27 crores and PAT 75% to INR16 crores, while H1 revenue grew only 5% after a weak Q1 that management attributed to component price volatility and supply uncertainty. Management said it went slow in Q1 as a prudent measure and has since geared up. Unexecuted order book is about INR1,420 crores (2.8x FY26 revenue), including a roughly INR600 crore Maharashtra order won in late Q2 with a two-year execution period. Management guided FY27 full-year growth in line with FY26, with H2 seasonally heavier.

segments.commentary: About 6% of the unexecuted order book; a segment entered in roughly the last one and a half years. Management said transmission has longer site-readiness lags (RoW, component availability) than distribution.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year growth expected to be in line with FY26, per management qualitative guidance; H2 seasonally heavier.

Year-end FY27 order book targeted at about INR1,500-2,000 crores, dependent on wins in two to three new states, with bids of about INR1,000-1,500 crores planned and a historical success rate of about 30%.

Company has said underground cabling is only about 20% complete nationally, with future growth expected in Tier B and C cities.
demand_pricing: Q2 margin improvement attributed to revenue mix: higher commissioning and erection work plus final milestone billings on completed orders.
Price escalation clauses with no ceiling are in tenders, with monthly back-to-back escalation from the funding agency, per management.

Management said there have been no project delays or liquidated damages historically.
Bill-to-order-book conversion historically about 70-80%+ (per management).

qa_highlights.question: How much order inflow was added in Q2 and what is the guidance for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR900-950 crores of new orders were added over the last six months, including a roughly INR600 crore Maharashtra order at end-Q2 (part of the INR1,420 crore book, two-year execution). Full-year growth expected in line with FY26, with execution visible mainly in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin increase and is 14% the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin was a function of revenue mix, with more commissioning and erection work and final milestone billings. Management expects margins to normalise to around 14% on a full-year basis, without exact quantitative guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 decline and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was weak due to peak component price volatility and supply uncertainty, so the company deliberately slowed work. Management said annual working capital needs should be roughly equal to H1 requirement, as working capital eases in H2 with government budget clearances.

qa_highlights.question: How will finance costs be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Near term, IPO proceeds should reduce debt over the next two to four quarters. Longer term, the company is rated BBB+ and aims for an A- upgrade, and a shift from bank guarantees to surety bonds is expected to lower funding costs and working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order-book breakup and do margins differ by vertical?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution about 85%, renewable about 8%, transmission about 6%. Orders are typically bundled across substations, cabling, instrumentation and RMUs, so margins were not split by vertical.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is executable in the next 6-12 months and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the historical bill-to-order ratio of 70-80%+ as the guide. No delays or liquidated damages historically; distribution has shorter site-readiness lags than transmission.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin is at risk from cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply inputs are protected by contract price variation clauses; labour volatility is limited. It pointed to a track record of maintained margin discipline over four to five years.

qa_highlights.question: Are RDSS and other schemes driving the pipeline, and how is the company positioned for digital and DER work?
qa_highlights.answer: RDSS is currently active only in Rajasthan and Gujarat; the Maharashtra order is ADB-funded and Himachal and West Bengal are World Bank-funded. RDSS phase 2 is announced, with tenders expected soon. The company is not currently pursuing SCADA or AMI work, but has quoted a BESS tender.

544959|2026-06.headline: Runwal Enterprises Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 3,400 million (from Rs 4,462 million) on occupation-certificate-based recognition, while pre-sales rose ~5% to Rs 4,835 million.
544959|2026-06.overview: This was the maiden earnings call after the company's listing, with the IPO proceeds received in the first week of October 2026. Pre-sales rose about 5% YoY to Rs 4,835 million and collections rose to Rs 5,754 million from Rs 4,993 million. Revenue from operations declined to about Rs 3,400 million, which management attributed to revenue being recognised only on occupation certificate and possession. Management said debt has been cut to about Rs 1,900 million external debt post-IPO and debt-to-equity has fallen from about 3 to about 1.5, with fuller benefits visible from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company issue stated guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna Kanodia said no specific guidance yet, but a general direction on growth (20-25% pre-sales) will be given while maintaining balance-sheet and margin health.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment plan and current debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said debt-to-equity fell from 3.1x to 1.5x and debt is now about Rs 1,900 crore external. Future borrowing will be limited and self-liquidating. Shashi Bhushan added that land monetisation to data operators is being considered, with JLL mandated and 10-12 interested parties.

qa_highlights.answer: Shashi Bhushan said the land is in Dombivli (Gardens and My City, part of a 250-acre parcel); about 18 acres is being considered for sale. No transaction has been concluded.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the IPO size cut from Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 500 crore?

570004|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of sales.
570004|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR1,800 crore versus about INR1,750 crore a year earlier, with Hi-Tech up about 8% and plastics down slightly. Consolidated EBITDA grew about 7% and margin rose to 13.2% from 12.8%, with Hi-Tech margin at 19.8% versus 17.5%. For FY26, revenue grew about 11% and Hi-Tech grew over 20%, while plastics grew only 2.4%. Reported PAT was negative at about INR40 crore due to one-time deferred tax unwinding, a Labour Code charge and non-cash NCD unwinding; management cited adjusted PAT of about INR133 crore. Management says debt repayments due in September and March FY27 are to be met from internal accruals and government receivables, with refinancing and equity as backups.

segments.name: Hi-Tech (drip irrigation, tissue culture, solar agri pumps)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 8% and EBITDA up about 22%, margin 19.8%. FY26 revenue grew more than 20%. Domestic business grew about 12% and retail about 13%, below the company's 15%-plus target because of March sales loss.

segments.name: Plastics (piping, plastic sheets)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue slightly down, EBITDA up 3.3%, margin 10.2% versus 9.7%. FY26 revenue grew only 2.4% and EBITDA declined. Overseas plastic sheet business is doing reasonably well.

segments.name: Agro Processing / Food

Gold loans: average blended yield is about 11% to 12%, with agri PSL benefit possibly taking it to 11.25%. Gold loans are about 30% of advances, against an internal ceiling of 30% to 35%.

Deposit pricing: time deposit rates were raised 40 bp during the quarter to fund front-loaded advances. FCNR(B) pricing is at about 7%, targeting tickets below USD1 million; base is about USD130 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth stay 100-200 bp above system if system growth has moved to around 18%?

qa_highlights.question: Why did SME YoY growth slow to 12-13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 was flat because the bank avoided pricing competition and some weak accounts. Q1 growth recovered to 6% QoQ, with commercial disbursements up 45% YoY on NTB plus ETB. Management expects about 18% growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS disbursement and pipeline?

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan blended yield?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank pushing a higher fixed-rate book if costs are rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed-rate loans at 11% to 15% insulate yields if rates fall later, and 20 to 30 bp of cost increase is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about full-year NIM given the Q2 guidance?

qa_highlights.question: How will the normalisation of write-off recoveries affect ROA over the next 2 to 3 years?

590003|2026-09.headline: KVB Q2 FY27: net profit INR788 crores (+37% YoY), NIM held at 4.26%, credit cost 0.43%, and advances growth guided to 18-20% for FY27.
590003|2026-09.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported a strong Q2 FY27 with net profit of INR788 crores, up 4% QoQ and 37% YoY, and operating profit of INR1,162 crores (+14% YoY, +6% QoQ). Total business reached INR2,39,712 crores (+5% QoQ, +18% YoY), with advances up 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores and deposits up 5% QoQ to INR1,28,123 crores. Management guided to 18-20% credit growth, NIM of 4% plus, ROA of about 2% and GNPA below 1.5% for FY27, while flagging that funding costs and loan-yield competition may pressure margins in coming quarters. Management also said the write-off recovery contribution has fallen sharply, and that the bank will rely more on core earnings.

financial_highlights.change: +INR1 crore QoQ; AS-15 provisions lower by INR28 crores

financial_highlights.value: 0.43% annualised (INR94 crores NPA/standard/restructured + INR25 crores floating provision)

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Grew 5% QoQ led by mortgages (+12% QoQ) and personal loans (+11% QoQ); retail jewel loans fell 1% to a total jewel book of INR32,153 crores (29% of advances), with LTV of 67% for agri gold and 59% for non-agri gold.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional
segments.commentary: Portfolio grew 12% QoQ (14% of advances), with average ticket size of INR42 crores; credit substitutes grew about INR500 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Commercial business (SBG and BBG)
segments.commentary: Grew 8% QoQ, with disbursements up about 24% QoQ; tailor-made products (GST surrogate, open term loan) crossed INR450 crores outstanding.

segments.name: Deposits and CASA
segments.commentary: Deposits up 5% QoQ; CASA rose INR1,489 crores in Q2 (current accounts +INR592 crores, savings +INR897 crores); retail term deposits 73% of total deposits, growing 6% QoQ (+INR3,902 crores).

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri loans grew 4% QoQ; agri jewel loans are 92% of the agri book.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 18-20% for FY27 (YTD 13%); management cautioned that YTD growth is not an indicator for full-year growth.
NIM for FY27 guided at 4% plus; management said it expects to cross 4% for the next 2 quarters but would not commit to 4.26% being retained.
ROA for FY27 guided at about 2%, with 2.1% reported for Q2.
GNPA guided below 1.5%, NNPA below 1%, slippages below 1%; cost-to-income expected below 45% over the next 2 quarters.
Branch expansion: 50 branches planned for FY27, with 26 to be opened by end-December 2026 and the balance by year-end.
Liquidity coverage ratio to be maintained in the 115-120% range versus 129% reported.
capex_capacity: 20 branches opened in H1 FY27 (including 2 in Q1); 50 planned for FY27.
Branch expansion focus: South India first, then Maharashtra and Gujarat, then Central and North, and East last.
Working capital utilisation steady at 76-79% over 1-1.5 years; US-export textile borrowers at about 55-56% utilisation.
Management sees little customer capex or textile modernisation demand currently.
demand_pricing: Credit demand in corporate and institutional segment came from EPC, infrastructure, commercial real estate, capital market participants and selective textile and NBFC capex.
Textile portfolio is about 5% of advances; split is 40% upstream (spinning/ginning), 22% midstream, 38% downstream (finished goods and apparel), with downstream most exposed to US tariffs.
Bank is seeing poaching in mortgages from banks offering lower rates; management chose not to match and accepted some account losses, while housing loans were also de-emphasised.
Vehicle loans trending down as a tactical choice: higher delinquency, 150% risk weight, and funding tightness; funds redirected to gold and mortgages.

Management expects pricing competition from banks flush with FCNR-driven liquidity, which may bring down yields; EBLR book rose to 57% of advances from 55%, fixed-rate book 34%, MCLR book fell to 7% from 9%.
Yield on investments fell 4 bps to 6.79%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any stress in gold loans given rising gold loan NPAs seen in bureau data for some peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen stress on the ground. It tightened margin-call monitoring over the last 1.5 years via a digitised system with a centralised cell, and says auctions are few because customers bring family ornaments and top up or repay. Retail gold is priced at about 14%, agri gold at 10.75%.

qa_highlights.question: How much bancassurance income is at risk from the proposed IRDA commission changes, and how will it be recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated commissions could fall 60-70% in some cases. It said LI penetration of about 1.6% would need to rise to 3.8-3.9% to make up the lost income, implying roughly 50% recoupment needed, and it is reworking product mix and penetration, which ranges from 0.9% to 2.2-2.3% across geographies.

qa_highlights.question: How resilient are non-core income sources (treasury and write-off recoveries) to ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury contributed 0.06% of the Dupont in both Q1 and Q2. Write-off recovery fell to 0.21% of Dupont from 0.65-0.9% earlier. Management said ROA would still be around 2% if recoveries fall another 10 bps, and that the bank has a pool of about INR2,500 crores of assets to recover from.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total stock of floating and contingency provisions, and what is the split?
qa_highlights.answer: Total provisions are 1.65% of advances including standard and floating; excluding them it is about 1.0-1.04%. Floating provision is INR100 crores (ECL-related, two years ago) plus INR25 crores added this quarter, on top of standard and restructured provisions. Restructured-book provision cover is 40.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the corporate and SME demand driven by working capital drawdown or capex, and what is the textile utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital utilisation is steady at 76-79% over 1-1.5 years. US-export textile borrowers are at 55-56% utilisation, and capex demand is limited. Textile is about 5% of advances, split 40% upstream, 22% midstream and 38% downstream. Growth comes from takeovers and fresh acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RWA rise and what is driving the vehicle loan decline?
qa_highlights.answer: RWA density moved to 58% from a 65% target, driven by selective NBFC exposure (150% risk weight if the bank is not in the rating), corporate growth, consumer credit (125% risk weight), and unhedged FX provisions. Vehicle loans are declining as a tactical call due to fixed rates, dealer commissions, high delinquency, 150% risk weight and deposit tightness; funds moved to gold and mortgages.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins trend down from 4.26%, and what is the repricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to retaining 4.26%. It expects 4%+ for the next 2 quarters, citing gold loan repricing from MCLR to fixed now complete, corporate yields of 9%+, and possible 3-6 month pricing pressure. EBLR book is about 56-57%, with working capital repricing 25 bps immediately.

Non-core income dependence: write-off recoveries fell to 0.21% of Dupont from 0.65-0.9%, and treasury contributed 0.06%; ROA guidance depends on core earnings.

Regulatory: pending IRDA bancassurance commission changes could cut income 60-70% in some cases; ECL transition timing still being assessed (about 1-1.5 months more clarity), with a 1.65% provision cover.
Leadership: CEO succession search committee formed; the current MD's tenure is under two years.

590013|2026-03.headline: Xpro Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR134.37 crore (vs INR158.2 crore) while PBT rose to INR16 crore; FY26 PBT fell to INR41 crore on forex loss and pre-operating costs.
590013|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR134.37 crore against INR158.2 crore a year earlier, while quarterly PBT rose to INR16 crore from INR11.5 crore. Full-year net revenue fell 5.6% to INR505.5 crore and production fell 5% to 31,335 MT, driven by lower Coex (refrigerator sheet and liner) volumes. Full-year PBT fell to INR41 crore from INR58 crore, hit by competitive pricing, input cost volatility, a forex loss of INR11 crore (INR11.14 crore unrealised) and pre-operating costs. The new Barjora dielectric film line entered commercial production on 27 March 2026, and management said polymer prices are rising steeply after the West Asia crisis.

qa_highlights.answer: Mix moved to 71% Biax and 29% Coex from 75:25 a year earlier, because Coex fell. Management said any inventory gain is short-term and that price increases will flow through later as inventory turns.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is expected on the new Barjora line?

qa_highlights.question: When will the RAK (UAE) line start and what volumes are expected in FY27 and FY28?

qa_highlights.question: Biggest concerns for FY28 sales volumes: raw materials, pricing or new entrants?

rows.why: Barjora dielectric line already in commercial production since 27 Mar 2026 (~INR240 crore capitalised), and RAK UAE plant trial production targeted Aug-Sep 2026 with commercial operations by Q3 FY27 (slipped from June 2026).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets at least 50% utilisation on the new Barjora line in FY27 'if not more' and full utilisation of the India lines next year, versus FY26 production down 5% to 31,335 MT from 33,014 MT, so the base is depressed and Coex demand is recovering from a temporary slowdown.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management stated no further new line is expected to be capitalised in FY27 and Coex capex is modest and routine; INR74.63 crore of QIP/preferential proceeds are idle, but no new project has been named and Biax capacity was described as capped by available capacity, so a further line is plausible but not guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance was given for FY27 and management declined to provide figures; FY26 revenue fell 5.6% to INR505.5 crore and PBT fell to INR41 crore from INR58 crore, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: RAK commercial start has already slipped from June 2026 to Q3 FY27, and West Asia polymer supply, shipping and forex (INR11 crore FY26 loss) risks are repeatedly flagged, with the Barjora ramp target of 50% not yet proven.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ultrathin and hazy films for capacitors, EV and railway uses are being validated with customers, where validation takes zero to many months; domestic ultrathin consumption is negligible but growing, and weighted average thickness is expected to move to about 4-5 micron within 2-3 years.

rows.label: Polymer-linked price increases on dielectric films
rows.why: Management said prices are moving up almost every alternate week with modal prices above INR550/kg after the West Asia crisis, and the company held prices lower earlier to anticipate new capacity, so pass-through is being pursued though elasticity may limit it.

rows.label: UAE (Ras Al Khaimah) subsidiary commercial start
rows.why: Trial production expected August-September 2026 with commercial operations targeted by Q3 FY27 barring unforeseen circumstances, and UAE line expected above 50% utilisation in FY28; subsidiary absorbed AED 4.52 million loss and received USD 9 million fresh equity.

rows.label: Girish Behal to become Managing Director
rows.why: Board has announced the appointment subject to shareholder approval; no fundamental impact is quantified in the brief.

tone.note: Management was confident on structural dielectric film demand and the Barjora ramp, but cautious and evasive on FY27 guidance, margins, pricing and utilisation, repeatedly citing West Asia and polymer uncertainty; analysts pressed on inventory gains, margin for the new line, and price sustainability

590051|2026-03.headline: Saksoft Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% YoY to INR 249 crore, with FY26 crossing INR 1,000 crore; management says pipeline is at a record ~USD 25 million.
590051|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR 249 crore, up roughly 4% YoY and down about 0.8% QoQ, while EBITDA grew 24% YoY to INR 45 crore at an 18.19% margin. FY26 revenue was about INR 1,007 crore (up ~14%), EBITDA INR 187 crore (18.57% margin) and net profit INR 133 crore (up 23%). Management said decision-making by customers has slowed amid AI-related uncertainty, though the pipeline has grown sharply, and it guided to 30% growth as a stretch target with 14-15% as the floor. Management was clear that the AI theme is pervasive, and it expects some margin compression near term from AI-driven renewal price cuts.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue)
segments.commentary: Americas ~50%, Europe 29%, Asia Pacific and other regions 21%.

segments.name: Vertical (FY26 revenue)
segments.commentary: Emerging Verticals 47% (high-tech and telecom), Banking & Financial Services ~31%, Logistics 14%, Commerce 8%.

segments.name: Delivery mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Onsite 44%, offshore 56%. Technical headcount 2,277 of 2,494 total at quarter end; utilization 83% for FY26 (excluding trainees).

segments.name: Customers
segments.commentary: Around 16 customers at USD 1 million+ revenue. Top 10 clients ~58% of revenue (per analyst question); top 20 clients ~70% of revenue (per management).

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to 30% growth in FY27 but said it is a 'tough call'; it expects 14-15% as the bare minimum and would put more money on 14-15%.
EBITDA margin: management aims to maintain the 17-18% range, but flagged a 'little bit of a dip' from AI investment and AI-driven price cuts at contract renewal.
Management expects growth to pick up as decision-making improves, targeting Q1 and Q2 FY27 for that pick-up.
Target of USD 500 million revenue by 2030; management says no significant capex is needed, funded by internal cash generation.
No guidance given on bottom-line margin for next year.
Headcount growth expected to be less than proportional to revenue growth; management sees utilization capped at about 85% due to the bench needed for agents and projects.
capex_capacity: Management says no significant capex is needed to reach USD 500 million by 2030; investment is in people and technology, funded by cash generation.
Continued investment in AI capabilities, accelerators and training of developers, project managers and leads on multiple LLMs.
Front-end investment: Chief Growth Officer in the US in place for about 9-10 months; Chief Growth Officer for UK and Europe joining end of June 2026.
Utilization (excluding trainees) of 83% for FY26; management sees 85% as the practical ceiling.
Technical employees fell about 4.5% in FY26 and total headcount about 5%, per analyst figures.
demand_pricing: Pipeline at about USD 25 million, the highest ever, versus about USD 5 million six months earlier; management credits a new US Chief Growth Officer and concerted sales effort.
Decision-making is slower; in Q3 two large customers deferred spending; in Q4 one resumed and the other is still deferring.
95-98% of growth and pipeline is from existing customers; management targets wallet share in top 20 accounts and says they could alone reach USD 500 million.
Vendor consolidation offers of 25-30% cost reduction are being used to win larger deals; Commerce is the smallest pipeline vertical.
Outcome-based billing is about 10% of revenue; the rest is time and material. Management is pushing outcome-based models and expects AI to reshape team composition.
Of FY26 growth of ~14%, management said ~3 points were currency (rupee depreciation); the rest came from volume growth at existing clients, not price.
Management expects some renewal price compression as customers seek AI productivity gains, with cannibalisation within contracts but overall spend expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Has sequential growth picked up back to the 3.5-4% QoQ range after two flattish quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is picking up but customer decisions are deferred due to AI noise; it expects Q1 and Q2 FY27 to see decisions pick up, with a record pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Would acquisitions be possible given the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions would be funded from internal accruals with maybe some borrowing; the maximum size considered is a target with top line of INR 100 crore. Nothing is imminent this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can 17-18% EBITDA margins be sustained in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will try to maintain them but expects a possible dip from AI investment and renewal price cuts; it sees no major concern.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a headcount decline and utilization rise toward 90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilization is capped at about 85% (agents may be counted in utilization); headcount will not scale linearly with revenue if AI adoption happens.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% growth target realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30% is a stretch; 14-15% is the bare minimum, and it would expect around 15% even if the rupee appreciates somewhat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall to about INR 12 crore in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the prior-year figure included a bad-debt provision for a US customer that went bust; no significant provisions were made in FY26, and the current run-rate should broadly continue.

risks_watch: Customer decision-making delays tied to AI uncertainty could keep sequential growth flat; watch Q1 and Q2 FY27 conversion of the USD 25 million pipeline.
Client concentration: top 10 clients ~58% of revenue, top 20 ~70%; loss of a large account would hit growth.
Margin pressure from AI-driven price cuts at renewal and from investment; management said AI costs could exceed human costs and remains an open variable.
Rupee depreciation contributed ~3 points of FY26 growth; a stronger rupee would reduce reported growth.

Structural risks flagged in Q&A: GCC insourcing (management says relevant mainly for large enterprises), cannibalisation of contracts, and the shift from time and material to outcome-based pricing (~10% today).
Ask on FY26 other expenses: the low Q4 level is partly due to the absence of the prior-year bad-debt provision, so the run-rate should be verified next quarter.
590051|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on pipeline strength and long-term AI positioning, but cautious on near-term growth, citing deferred customer decisions and AI-related uncertainty. Management openly called 30% growth a stretch and steered expectations to 14-15%. It was evasive on AI revenue disclosure and declined to give margin guidance.
key_quotes: Our pipeline is really strong. I would say it's probably the strongest it's ever been in the last in the history of the company.
We are shooting for 30% growth. Now will 30% happen? It' s going to be a tough call.
Our top 20 customers give us about 70% of our revenue, okay?
So even if we were to get no new logo, we could achieve that $500 million just by increasing wallet share in these 20 accounts.

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and bank balance (31 Mar 2026)

financial_highlights.value: INR 0.55 per share (55% of face value INR 1); total 100% for the year

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management aims to hold the 17-18% EBITDA margin (FY26 18.57%) but flagged a 'little bit of a dip' from AI investment and renewal price cuts, so compression is more likely than expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says no significant capex is needed to reach USD 500 million by 2030 and utilisation (83% FY26) is capped at about 85%, so no new capacity is signalled; growth is to come from headcount-light delivery.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pipeline is at about USD 25 million versus about USD 5 million six months earlier, 95-98% from existing clients, and FY26 growth of ~14% was volume-led; management targets 14-15% as the floor, with 30% as a stretch.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no significant capex is needed and utilisation is 83% with a practical ceiling of 85%, so a capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management calls 30% a stretch and 14-15% the floor; upside depends on Q1-Q2 FY27 conversion of the USD 25 million pipeline, which is still being deferred by some customers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Two large customers deferred spending in Q3 and one was still deferring in Q4, and AI renewal price cuts could pull growth toward the 14-15% floor or below it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Product or service launches were not discussed; AI investment is in people, accelerators and training rather than named offerings.

rows.label: Pipeline conversion of USD 25 million
rows.why: Pipeline rose from about USD 5 million six months earlier to about USD 25 million, but one of two deferring customers was still deferring in Q4, so conversion depends on decisions resuming.

rows.label: AI-driven renewal price cuts
rows.why: Management expects some renewal price compression as customers seek AI productivity gains, with vendor consolidation offers of 25-30% cost reduction being used to win larger deals.

rows.label: Other expenses run-rate
rows.why: Q4 other expenses fell to about INR 12 crore because the prior-year bad-debt provision was absent; the run-rate needs verification next quarter and a recurrence would weigh on margin.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record pipeline and AI positioning but cautious on near-term growth, calling 30% a stretch and steering to 14-15%; analysts pressed on utilisation, headcount, margin sustainability and the other-expense run-rate.

590051|2026-06.headline: Saksoft Q1 FY27 revenue flat at about INR 249 crore, EBITDA INR 45 crore (18.26% margin); FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore held.
590051|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was about INR 249 crore, broadly flat year on year, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (down 1% YoY) and PAT of about INR 29 crore (11.78% margin). Management said demand softness that began in Q3 FY26 continued, with top clients delaying renewals and decisions. Pipeline is stated to be far larger than the USD 25 million cited last quarter, now about USD 28 million, but conversion is slow. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore (about 25% growth on FY26's INR 1,007 crore) while saying Q2 looks muted and growth is expected in H2.

financial_highlights.change: flat, per management, as revenue is flat
headcount declining over last two quarters per analyst
management target at least 65% in 2-3 years

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Americas 52% of revenue, Europe 27%, Asia Pacific and other 21%.

segments.name: Delivery mix
segments.commentary: Onsite 43%, offshore 57%.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Emerging verticals 45%, BFSI about 30%, transportation and logistics about 16%, digital commerce 9%. Management expects growth in emerging verticals first, then BFSI and logistics; digital commerce sees the most headwinds. BFSI revenue flat in absolute terms Q4 to Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore maintained; management will restate at end of Q2 if needed.
Next quarter (Q2 FY27) expected to remain muted; management hopeful of growth in H2 FY27.
Management expects headcount to flatten or decline while revenue grows, driven by AI productivity and shift to outcome-based and managed services.
Management expects employee and resource costs as a percentage of revenue to decline over time; about 77% of costs are employee plus contractor costs, with appraisals impacting next quarter.
Management claims AI gives 30-50% efficiency in product engineering and 20-30% in managed services, per management rule of thumb.
Long-term target of INR 500 million (analyst cited FY30) was referenced but management focused on FY27 only.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning details were discussed.
Headcount reduction attributed to AI-driven engineering productivity, AI agents replacing recruitment and invoicing/payables roles, and move away from headcount-linked contracts.
demand_pricing: Management says pipeline is at a record level, now about USD 28 million versus USD 25 million last quarter, with quality improved by a shift to bigger managed-services and outcome-based deals.
Decision-making is delayed; top clients face near-term pressures. Management says nothing is normalizing, though it expects recovery in medium term.
Company deliberately avoids headcount/body-shop deals, which is causing near-term revenue pain.
Company is exiting tail accounts without potential to scale; exact number of accounts let go to be sent later.
Competition has increased as larger IT players bid for smaller deals, but management says mid-sized firms are gaining access to bigger RFPs because of AI.
New logo added in first month by new Chief Growth Officer for Europe: a logistics/airline company that is a major supplier to Amazon.
AI: company does not track AI revenue separately; management says all projects contain AI components and none are pilots.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline now versus last quarter, and when will conversion and growth show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pipeline is about USD 28 million versus USD 25 million last quarter, with better quality. Next quarter looks muted, with growth hoped for in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR 1,200-1,250 crore, about 25% growth on INR 1,007 crore in FY26, and will restate at end of Q2 if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals drive growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Emerging verticals first, then BFSI and logistics. Digital commerce has the most headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost falling and what will new senior hires add?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount falls from AI productivity, AI agents in support functions, and a shift to outcome-based deals. Two senior hires were funded by repurposing costs of founders who exited after earnouts, so management does not expect employee cost to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company letting go of tail clients, and how is client concentration changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is exiting accounts without scale potential. Top 10 concentration fell from 58% to 56%, and it has no target to reduce it further.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue comes from AI and what is the AI deal-size trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not break out AI revenue. It said every project includes AI, and pure AI work is limited to AI co-innovation labs.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from the US and how will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: US share is 52% (management corrected from 55%), with a target of at least 65% in two to three years.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted, and FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore requires a sharp H2 recovery from a flat H1.
Deal conversion is slow as the shift to larger outcome-based deals lengthens decision cycles.
Digital commerce faces the most headwinds, and BFSI revenue is flat QoQ.
Management did not quantify the number of accounts exited; it promised to send figures later. Pipeline figure of USD 28 million is also to be confirmed in writing.
Long-term INR 500 million target (FY30) was raised by an analyst but not addressed by management.
Competition from larger IT players moving down into smaller deals.
Appraisals next quarter could push up employee costs.
590051|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term demand and conversion, with management openly saying Q2 will be muted and that they do not expect improvement soon. It is more confident on the medium-term pipeline, AI productivity and the move to managed services, but it gave few hard numbers beyond the FY27 guidance it reiterated.
key_quotes: Decision making is getting delayed unfortunately, and we are pushing as hard as we can, but there is a limit to how much you can fight the industry
Numbers will come, growth will come, it won't happen overnight.
Nothing is normalizing.
Nothing is pilot, everything is in production.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin held at 18.26% with headcount falling and management expecting employee and resource costs as a share of revenue to decline over time, but appraisals next quarter could push costs up.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue was flat YoY at about INR 249 crore and Q2 is guided muted, so growth depends on a sharp H2 recovery from the USD 28 million pipeline (up from USD 25 million) converting.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 83% but management discussed no capex and is shifting to AI productivity and headcount reduction, not new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore (about 25% growth) was only held, and H1 is flat, so an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Flat H1 against a guide needing about 25% growth means a sharp H2 recovery is required, and management said it will restate at end of Q2 if needed.

rows.label: Pipeline rise to USD 28 million with slow conversion
rows.why: Pipeline rose from USD 25 million to about USD 28 million, but management says conversion is slow and decisions are delayed, with growth expected in H2.

rows.label: US share target of at least 65% from 52%
rows.why: US share is 52% of revenue today against a stated target of at least 65% in 2-3 years, but no interim numbers were given.

rows.label: Headcount reduction from AI productivity
rows.why: Management expects headcount to flatten or decline while revenue grows, with 2,434 employees today and headcount already falling over the last two quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term pipeline, AI productivity and the shift to managed services, but cautious on near-term demand, saying Q2 will be muted. Analysts pushed on the FY27 guidance, the pipeline conversion and the headcount decline.
